body:
## Parents and dependencies

- #1574 — editor/LSP usable-alpha authority
- #2528 — accepted current-main packaged editor composition
- #2927 — shared durable `RepairAttempt` authority
- #1613 — front-door/workflow discovery
- #1661 / #1663 — typed action data and shared fix-instruction projection
- #1702 / #1579 — measured real-client repair attempts

## Release disposition

Post-`0.11.0` product-convergence work unless the release authority explicitly promotes a bounded compatibility-only slice. Exact `0.11.0` editor qualification remains #2423/#2769 and must not wait for this new UX shell.

## Problem

The packaged VS Code extension now proves the default Rust, explicit full-seam, preview, untrusted-workspace, lifecycle, and packaging journeys. The visible interaction still exposes many internal operations as peer-level commands: packets, briefs, context, verify routes, receipts, reports, status lenses, and refresh variants.

The CLI already has a two-phase repair driver, and #2927 will turn it into a durable transaction. VS Code should become a contextual shell over that same attempt—not a second editor-specific repair state machine.

## Required outcome

Provide one primary editor journey:

```text
current actionable diagnostic
→ Start Repair
→ shared RepairAttempt created
→ exact related test/fix site opened
→ external human/agent test edit
→ Continue or Finish Repair
→ shared after/verify/receipt authority
→ Problems/status shows closed, improved, unchanged, regressed, limited, stale, incomparable, or failed
```

CLI and editor must project one attempt identity, producer evidence, edit cage, movement result, and receipt chain.

## Primary visible command shell

The ordinary palette/onboarding surface should emphasize approximately:

```text
ripr: Show Status
ripr: Start or Continue Repair
ripr: Refresh Full Analysis
ripr: Open Report
ripr: Diagnose Setup
```

This is a discoverability hierarchy, not command deletion.

Existing packet, brief, context, verify, receipt, first-PR, navigation, and diagnostic commands remain:

- contextual actions on the current diagnostic or attempt;
- advanced palette commands where appropriate;
- compatibility routes for existing users and agents.

Do not maintain two command meanings for the same operation.

## Shared attempt contract

VS Code consumes #2927's manifest/DTO and does not reconstruct attempt state from clipboard contents, output-channel prose, Problems entries, or local extension-only files.

It must preserve:

```text
RepairAttemptId
root/repository/base/head/config/profile/input identity
gap/seam/canonical-item identity
allowed_edit_surface and must_not_change
related test/fix-site identity
before/after/verify/receipt identities
operational state
movement state
limitations/non_claims
next_action
```

The extension may retain presentation state, but repository/evidence authority stays in the shared attempt.

## Start Repair

From one current actionable diagnostic or status-selected gap:

1. validate Workspace Trust and current diagnostic/evidence identity;
2. call the canonical before-phase authority;
3. create exactly one shared attempt;
4. show a bounded summary:
   - gap and missing discriminator;
   - related test and exact fix site;
   - permitted edit surface and forbidden production surface;
   - attempt state and next action;
5. open the selected test/range when safe;
6. expose contextual packet/context/report actions;
7. never claim the issue is fixed merely because an editor opened.

A static-limited, stale, preview-limited, wrong-root, or unresolved-target item must remain a typed limitation and cannot start a repair-ready attempt.

## Continue or Finish Repair

The command should:

- resolve the explicit active attempt or ask the user to choose among several;
- call the shared after-phase authority;
- validate currentness and comparability;
- display the resulting movement and receipt state;
- refresh diagnostics/status from the same current evidence;
- retain precise recovery for stale, incomparable, limited, and failed results.

Repeated invocation is idempotent or returns an explicit already-complete result.

## Status and context

Status should foreground the attempt lifecycle:

```text
No current repair
Repair awaiting edit
Repair ready to finish
Repair improved
Repair closed
Repair unchanged
Repair regressed
Repair stale
Repair incomparable
Repair limited
Repair failed
```

For an active attempt, show only the current bounded next action first. Artifact inventory and lower-level commands remain available through details/report surfaces.

## Trust, lifecycle, and isolation

- Untrusted workspaces create, read, finish, or copy no repair authority.
- Root changes invalidate or visibly stale the attempt; no first-folder fallback.
- Session restart/deactivation preserves durable attempts without preserving stale in-memory authority.
- Repeated activation/restart leaves one client, one server, and one command-registration set.
- Several open workspaces/attempts never silently select the wrong root or attempt.
- Extension settings, editor selection, clipboard, and output channel are restored or isolated in tests.
- No extension-owned state can strengthen a shared limited/stale/incomparable result.

## Implementation slices

### PR A — shared attempt adapter and status projection

- consume #2927 manifest/DTO;
- add attempt-aware status and contextual current-attempt resolution;
- keep existing commands unchanged initially.

### PR B — Start Repair

- create the shared attempt from a current actionable diagnostic;
- open the exact related test/fix site;
- expose bounded contextual actions and trust/currentness failures.

### PR C — Continue/Finish Repair and visible shell

- finish through the shared after phase;
- project terminal movement and receipt states;
- simplify the primary palette/onboarding hierarchy while preserving advanced commands.

## Required proof

- trusted actionable Rust diagnostic starts one shared attempt;
- limited/stale/preview-unready/untrusted items cannot start one;
- exact test/fix site and edit cage agree with CLI/packet evidence;
- external edit followed by finish yields the same movement/receipt semantics as CLI;
- multiple attempts and roots require explicit selection;
- stale head/config/root after start fails visibly with restart route;
- restart/deactivation during an active attempt leaves no duplicate server/registration or lost durable manifest;
- no manual artifact path or clipboard handoff is required for the ordinary journey;
- source extension-host and extracted-VSIX journeys run on Linux/Xvfb and Windows where the existing package matrix applies;
- removal of the shared-attempt binding makes parity tests fail.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One primary command starts or continues the current repair without exposing internal artifact plumbing.
- [ ] CLI and editor use the same `RepairAttemptId`, evidence identities, movement states, and receipt authority.
- [ ] The extension has no parallel attempt lifecycle or currentness validator.
- [ ] Advanced packet/brief/verify/receipt commands remain available but no longer define the first-hour path.
- [ ] Workspace Trust, root identity, restart, stale state, and multiple-attempt behavior fail closed.
- [ ] #1702/#1579 can measure the editor journey using the same attempt receipt as CLI.

## Non-goals

- no automatic test generation;
- no `WorkspaceEdit` or source edit in this issue;
- no embedded model/provider;
- no verification-command execution or mutation execution;
- no support for unexercised editors;
- no replacement of standard diagnostics/hover/actions;
- no `0.11.0` candidate, version, source, tag, publication, signing, marketplace, or credential operation.

## Claim boundary

Completion makes the packaged VS Code extension a contextual human shell over the same durable repair transaction used by the CLI. It does not prove analyzer correctness, test adequacy, or broad real-repository usefulness without #1702/#1579.
